what: The plasticity-amendment ledger read by ledger_bridge.py. Each amendment prescribes ONE plasticity parameter value for the NEXT experiment run. This is the machine-readable half of the covenant ledger as it is reachable from this repository (the prose half is docs/RETRACTED.json and prereg/*.md); it lives in docs/ beside RETRACTED.json and CLAIMS_INDEX.json. The bridge is strictly one-directional (ledger -> net config); nothing writes an amendment here automatically -- amendments are added by hand, with a cited source, so the loop's effect can be audited.

schema.id: short unique id, e.g. SE-A1 (A for amendment)
schema.kind: optional; omit (or 'scientific') for a real amendment. 'mechanism_exercise' is a separate, visible class that exercises the parse->config path WITHOUT being a plasticity finding: the bridge never selects it for a run (latest_plasticity_amendment and run_trial ignore it), and it MUST cite nothing (source 'none'). Enforced by ledger_bridge.py.
schema.source: the standing record this amendment derives from: a prereg id, an SE-R retraction id, or an SE-K claim id in this repo. ENFORCED, not just documented: ledger_bridge.py reads docs/RETRACTED.json and REFUSES any scientific amendment whose source is retracted (e.g. SE-R3) or missing, so a retracted citation can never activate a parameter change. For a mechanism_exercise entry this must be the literal 'none'.
schema.param: exactly one of: 'tau_plus_ms' (the STDP taupre, baseline 20 ms) or 'background_rate_hz' (the PoissonGroup noise rate, baseline 5 Hz)
schema.value: the prescribed numeric value, in the unit named by param
schema.rationale: one line: why this value, tied to the source

note: amendments is EMPTY by design. No plasticity amendment has been registered: SE-R3 (docs/RETRACTED.json) WITHDREW the claim that the ~1.9x ratio pointed to a change in the plasticity rule, so there is no standing source that prescribes a tau_plus or background-rate value. While this list is empty, ledger_bridge.py ABORTS every run rather than falling back to the baseline -- fail-closed, by requirement. The baseline block above is a reference for amendment authors and for the config the FIRST run starts from; the bridge never treats it as an amendment. 2026-11-10, after an eleven-voice consult that was unanimous (ops/CONSULT_PLASTICITY_AMENDMENT in the covenant repo): keep it empty. The clean endpoint (burst-synapse selectivity, exp17) validates WHAT to measure, not a parameter value, so citing it to set tau_plus or the background rate would be evidence laundering. A legitimate amendment needs a STANDING result from a pre-registered sweep that scores a parameter against selectivity on fresh seeds; until such a sweep exists and the hypothesis is re-pre-registered around selectivity (prereg/PREREG_ledger_bridge.md), the honest state is empty and fail-closed. To exercise the loop meanwhile, use a kind:'mechanism_exercise' entry (source 'none'); it can never count as a finding.
